# Lantern Tide
### A quiet lighthouse-keeping game about storms, ships and second chances

(Fictional product written for the grounding evaluation set. It does not exist.)

**About the game**

Lantern Tide is a hand-painted management game set on a remote lighthouse island. You play Maren, a retired ferry pilot who takes over a failing lighthouse and has one winter to bring it back to life. Each night you choose which ships to guide, which repairs to make, and which storms to simply wait out.

**Key features**

- A full day-and-night cycle where every night lasts about 9 minutes of real time
- 36 hand-painted ships, each with its own captain and a short story told over radio
- Repair and upgrade the lamp, the foghorn and the supply dock in any order
- No combat and no fail state: a missed ship changes the story instead of ending it
- Estimated length of 10 to 12 hours, with a relaxed mode that removes all timers

**System requirements**

Minimum:
- OS: Windows 10 64-bit
- Processor: Intel Core i3-7100
- Memory: 4 GB RAM
- Graphics: Intel UHD 620
- Storage: 2 GB available space

**Early feedback (closed playtest, 42 players)**

> "The radio conversations are the best part. I wanted more of them." — Playtester 12

> "The first three nights are slow, and I nearly stopped before the storm system opened up." — Playtester 30

**Release information**

- Planned release: spring 2027
- Platforms: Steam (Windows and Steam Deck); a console version is not planned yet
- Planned price: $16.99
- Languages: English, French and Japanese (text only, no voice acting)

**From the developers**

We are a team of three working from two countries. This is our second game; our first one sold about 8,000 copies. We have been building Lantern Tide for 20 months and we will post a public demo before release.
